verses.h1: ولو لم يهجني الظاعنون لهاجني
verses.h2: حمائم ورق في الديار وقوع

verses.h1: تجاوبن فاستبكين من كان ذا هوى
verses.h2: نوائح لم تذرف لهن دموع

verses.h1: Is it because of an abandoned campsite in the hollow, Jaww Jalājil,
verses.h2: that your companion streams with tears and is distraught?

verses.h1: I defied love on the day at al-Qilāt, though on the day at al-Naqā I listened eagerly to love’s call.
A raging wind lingered there, drawing the east wind after it,
verses.h2: scattering, blowing dust about, and gathering it in heaps.

verses.h1: Will those days of ours return, O Mayy—
verses.h2: those at Dhū al-Rimth—or not? Is there no returning for them?

verses.h1: Even had the departing people not stirred my longing, it would have been stirred
verses.h2: by gray doves settled among the dwellings.

verses.h1: They answered one another, making everyone who had loved weep—
verses.h2: mourning birds for whom no tears flowed.

notes.note: Jaww Jalājil appears to name a hollow or tract of low ground associated with Jalājil; its precise location is uncertain.
The place names القلات and النقا are rendered al-Qilāt and al-Naqā; their precise locations, and the vocalization of the first, are uncertain.
تستدرج الصبا is rendered ‘drawing the east wind after it,’ but the precise image of the two winds interacting is uncertain.
The precise location of Dhū al-Rimth is uncertain.

verses.h1: سقى دمنتين لم نجد لهما مثلا
verses.h2: بحقل لكم يا عز قد زانتا حقلا

verses.h1: نجاء الثريا كل آخر ليلة
verses.h2: تجودهما جودا وتردفهما وبلا

verses.h1: إذا شحطت دار لعزة لم أجد
verses.h2: لها في الألى يلحين في وصلها مثلا

verses.h1: فيا ليت شعري والحوادث جمة
verses.h2: متى تجمع الأيام يوما بها شملا؟

verses.h1: May the two deserted campsites, whose like we have never found, be watered—
verses.h2: yours at Ḥaql, O ʿAzz, which have adorned Ḥaql—

verses.h1: by the rainclouds of al-Thurayyā at the close of every night,
verses.h2: drenching them generously, bringing downpour after downpour.

verses.h1: When ʿAzza’s dwelling lies far away, I find
verses.h2: no equal to her among the women who reproach me for loving her.

verses.h1: Would that I knew, amid so many turns of fortune,
verses.h2: when time will one day reunite me with her!

notes.note: Ḥaql is taken as a place-name; its precise location is uncertain.
نجاء الثريا is understood as rainclouds associated with al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades), though the precise sense of نجاء here is uncertain.

prose_translation.intro: And Kuthayyir ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:

poems.intro: وقال أرطاة بن كعب بن قعين:

verses.h1: يا دارة السلم التي شرقيها
verses.h2: دمن يظل حمامها يبكينا

verses.h1: ما كنت أول من تفرق شمله
verses.h2: ورأى الغداة من الفراق يقينا

verses.h1: O Dārat al-Salam, to whose east
verses.h2: lie old encampment traces whose doves keep making us weep!

verses.h1: I was not the first whose company was scattered,
verses.h2: who saw at dawn that parting was certain.

notes.note: Dārat al-Salam is an unidentified locality; the precise vocalization of السلم is uncertain.
يبكينا is read here as ‘makes us weep’; without vowel marks, it could also mean ‘weeps for us.’
The unvocalized كنت could mean ‘I was’ or ‘you were’; the translation adopts the first-person reading.

prose_translation.intro: And Arṭāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Quʿayn said:

verses.h1: خليلي عوجا حييا رسم دمنة
verses.h2: محتها الصبا بعدي وطارت خيامها

verses.h1: هل الدار إن عجنا
verses.h2: لك الخير ناطق بحاجتنا أطلالها وثمامها؟

verses.h1: ألا لا، ولكن عائد الشوق هاجه
verses.h2: عليك طلول قد أحال مقامها

verses.h1: منازل من مي بوهبين جادها
verses.h2: أهاضيب طل دجنها واتمهامها

verses.h1: My two friends, turn aside and greet the traces of a campsite
verses.h2: the east wind has erased since I left, whose tents have flown away.

verses.h1: The dwelling—if we turn aside,
verses.h2: bless you!—will its ruins and thumām-grass speak of what we seek?

verses.h1: No indeed! But longing has returned, stirred
verses.h2: for you by ruins whose site has grown old.

verses.h1: Dwellings of Mayy at Wahbayn, watered
verses.h2: by heavy showers, their clouds drizzling, and their [itmihmām].

notes.note: The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: لك الخير ناطق probably belongs at the end of the first hemistich. The translation preserves the supplied division.

عليك may mean longing stirred ‘for you,’ addressing the beloved, or longing stirred ‘in you.’ أحال مقامها may specifically mean that a year has passed over the site, rather than simply that it has grown old.
Wahbayn (وهبين) is treated as a place name, but its identification and vocalization are uncertain.

The wording طل دجنها واتمهامها is unclear and may be corrupted. ‘Their clouds drizzling’ tentatively takes طل as a verb. I cannot securely interpret اتمهامها and have left its central word provisionally transliterated in brackets.

verses.h1: ألمم على دمن تقادم عهدها
verses.h2: بالجزع واستلب الزمان جمالها

verses.h1: رسم لقاتلة الغرانق ما به
verses.h2: إلا الوحوش خلت له وخلا لها

verses.h1: ظلت تسائل بالمتيم أهله
verses.h2: وهي التي فعلت به أفعالها

verses.h1: Stop by the campsite traces, long since abandoned,
verses.h2: at al-Jizʿ, where time has stripped away their beauty.

verses.h1: A remnant of the dwelling of the slayer of handsome youths—nothing is there
verses.h2: but wild beasts, left alone with it, and it with them.

verses.h1: She kept asking his family about the love-stricken man,
verses.h2: though she herself had done to him all she had done.

notes.note: Al-Jizʿ may be a place-name or a topographical description meaning the bend or winding course of a valley.
الغرانق is understood here as handsome young men, whom the beloved figuratively slays; the word can also denote cranes.

prose_translation.intro: And Aḥmar ibn al-Ayham al-Taghlibī said:

verses.h1: دمن لزينب قبل تشريد النوى
verses.h2: من ذي الأراك بزينب ولعوب

verses.h1: تأبى المنازل أن تجيب ومن جوى
verses.h2: يوم الديار دعوت غير مجيب

verses.h1: فسقى الغضى والساكنيه وإن هم
verses.h2: شبوه بين جوانح وقلوب

verses.h1: Ruins of Zaynab’s camp, from before separation drove
verses.h2: Zaynab and Laʿūb away from Dhū al-Arāk.

verses.h1: The dwellings refuse to answer; out of heartache,
verses.h2: on my day at the dwellings, I called to one who gave no answer.

verses.h1: May al-Ghaḍā and those who dwelt there be watered, though they
verses.h2: kindled its fire within ribs and hearts.

notes.note: I take Laʿūb as a second woman’s name. The precise location of Dhū al-Arāk is uncertain.
Al-Ghaḍā may be a place-name or refer to a stand of ghaḍā trees. The following phrase, literally ‘they kindled it,’ evokes the burning of their wood.

poems.poet: علي بن أحمد بن أبي أمية
poems.poet_from_text: علي بن أحمد بن أبي أمية الكاتب
poems.intro: قال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني: لما قال علي بن أحمد بن أبي أمية الكاتب:

poet.expected: علي بن أحمد بن أبي أمية
poet.from_text: علي بن أحمد بن أبي أمية الكاتب

verses.h1: يا ريح ما تصنعين بالدمن
verses.h2: كم لك من محو منظر حسن

verses.h1: محوت آثارنا وأحدثت آ
verses.h2: ثارا بربع الحبيب لم تكن

verses.h1: إن تك يا ربع قد بليت من الر
verses.h2: يح، فإني بال من الحزن

verses.h1: قد كان يا ربع فيك لي سكن
verses.h2: فصرت مذبان بعده سكني

verses.h1: شبهت ما أبلت الرياح من آثار
verses.h2: حبيبي النائي إلى بدني

verses.h1: حاشاك يا ريح أن تكوني على ال
verses.h2: عاشق عونا لحادث الزمن

verses.h1: O wind, what are you doing to the traces of abandoned camps?
verses.h2: How many a lovely sight you have effaced!

verses.h1: You erased our traces and brought into being
verses.h2: traces at the beloved’s dwelling that were not there before.

verses.h1: If, O dwelling, you have been worn away by the wind,
verses.h2: I too am worn away by grief.

verses.h1: Once, O dwelling, you held one who was my solace;
verses.h2: since he departed, you have become my solace in his stead.

verses.h1: I likened the wind-worn traces
verses.h2: of my distant beloved to my own body.

verses.h1: Far be it from you, O wind, to be
verses.h2: an ally to time’s calamities against the lover.

notes.note: I read مذبان as مذ بان, ‘since he departed.’ سكن can mean a dwelling or someone who provides comfort; سكني in the second hemistich could therefore mean ‘my dwelling’ rather than ‘my solace.’
The construction شبهت ... إلى بدني is unusual: شبهت normally takes ب rather than إلى to introduce the object of comparison. I have understood it as ‘I likened ... to my body.’

prose_translation.intro: Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī said: When ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī Umayya, the secretary, recited:

poems.intro: كثر الناس فيه، وتداولوه، وغني فيه عمرو الغوال، فقال أبو موسى الأعمى:

verses.h1: يا رب خذني، وخذ عليا، وخذ
verses.h2: يا ريح ما تصنعين بالدمن

verses.h1: عجل إلى النار بالثلاثة والرا
verses.h2: بع عمرو الغوال في قرن

verses.h1: O Lord, take me, take ʿAlī, and take
verses.h2: “O wind, what are you doing to the traces of the encampments?”

verses.h1: Hasten the three to the Fire, and the fourth—
verses.h2: ʿAmr al-Ghawwāl—all bound together in one fetter.

notes.note: The second hemistich appears to quote the opening of the poem being mocked, making that poem the third object of “take.” I could not identify the quoted poem or establish who ʿAlī is.
The word الرابع (“the fourth”) is divided between the hemistichs; the translation places it wholly in h1. The singer’s epithet الغوال, rendered al-Ghawwāl, is uncertain and may be corrupt.

prose_translation.intro: People talked a great deal about it and passed it around, and ʿAmr al-Ghawwāl sang it. Then Abū Mūsā al-Aʿmā said:

verses.h1: متى تعرف العينان أطلال دمنة
verses.h2: لليلى بأعلى ذي معارك تدمعا

verses.h1: على النحر والسربال حتى تبله
verses.h2: سجوم، ولم تجزع إلى الدار مجزعا

verses.h1: خليلي عوجا اليوم نقض لبانة
verses.h2: وإلا تعوجا اليوم لا ننطلق معا

verses.h1: Whenever the eyes recognize the traces of a campsite,
verses.h2: Laylā’s, in upper Dhū Maʿarik, they weep—

verses.h1: Down over the breast and tunic, until it is drenched
verses.h2: With streaming tears, though you have not crossed over toward the dwelling.

verses.h1: My two friends, turn aside today: let us satisfy a longing;
verses.h2: If you do not turn aside today, we shall not set off together.

notes.note: Dhū Maʿarik appears to be a place-name; I cannot identify its location.
The construction ولم تجزع إلى الدار مجزعا is uncertain. I have taken تجزع in the sense of crossing or making one’s way, with an implied ‘you’; a sense connected with grief is also possible.

poems.intro: قال أبو عمرو: كان بيهس بن صهيب بن عامر بن عبد الله بن نائل يهوى امرأة من قومه يقال لها: "صفراء" وكان يتحدث إليها، ويجلس في بيتها، ويكثر وجده بها، ولا يظهره لأحد، ولا يخطبها إلى أبيها، لأنه كان صعلوكا لا مال له، وكان ينتظر أن يثرى، وكان شاعرا شجاعا، له مواقف مشهورة، وكان من أحسن الشباب وجها وشارة، وحديثا، وشعرا، فكان نساء الحي يتعرضن له، يجلسن إليه، ويتحدثن معه، فمرت به صفراء، فرأته جالسا مع فتاة منهن، فهجرته زمانا، لا تجيبه إذا دعاها، ولا تخرج إليه إذا زارها، وعرض له سفر، فخرج فيه، ثم عاد وقد زوجها أبوها رجلا من بني أسد، فأخرجها وانتقل بها عن ديارهم، فقال بيهس بن صهيب:

verses.h1: سقى دمنة صفراء كانت تحلها
verses.h2: نجاء الثريا طلها وذهابها

verses.h1: وجاد عليها كل أسحم هاطل
verses.h2: ولا زال مخضرا مريعا جنابها

verses.h1: أحب ثرى أرض إلي وإن نأت
verses.h2: محلك منها، نبتها وترابها

verses.h1: على أنها غضبى علي وحبذا
verses.h2: رضاها إذا ما أرضيت وعتابها

verses.h1: نظرت وقد زال الحمول، ووازنوا
verses.h2: بركوة والوادي وحنت ركابها

verses.h1: فقلت لأصحابي: أبا لقرب منهم
verses.h2: جرى الطير، أم نادى ببين غرابها!؟

verses.h1: May Ṣafrāʾ’s deserted campsite, where she used to dwell, be watered
verses.h2: by the Pleiades’ rain-clouds, their drizzle and gentle showers.

verses.h1: May every dark, pouring cloud drench it,
verses.h2: and may its grounds remain forever green and fertile.

verses.h1: The earth dearest to me, however far away,
verses.h2: is where you dwell—its plants and its soil.

verses.h1: Though she is angry with me, how sweet
verses.h2: her pleasure when she is appeased, and her reproaches.

verses.h1: I looked as the laden camels departed, and they drew abreast
verses.h2: of Rakwa and the valley, while her riding camels moaned.

verses.h1: I said to my companions: “Was it nearness to them
verses.h2: that the birds foretold, or did their raven cry out parting?”

notes.note: نجاء is understood as rain-clouds and ذهابها as gentle showers; the precise meteorological senses are uncertain.
Rakwa (ركوة) is an unidentified place; its vocalization is uncertain. الوادي is translated literally as “the valley,” though it might designate a particular named locality.
The printed أبا لقرب is read as أبالقرب (“was it nearness…?”), correcting an apparent word-spacing error.

prose_translation.intro: Abū ʿAmr said: Bayhas ibn Ṣuhayb ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Nāʾil loved a woman of his people called Ṣafrāʾ. He would converse with her and sit in her house. His passion for her was intense, but he revealed it to no one, nor did he ask her father for her hand, for he was a penniless man with no wealth and was waiting until he became prosperous. He was a poet and a brave man, with celebrated feats to his name, and was among the finest young men in looks, bearing, conversation, and poetry. The women of the tribe would seek his attention, sitting beside him and talking with him. Ṣafrāʾ passed by him and saw him sitting with one of these young women, so she shunned him for a time, neither answering when he called her nor coming out to him when he visited her. An occasion to travel arose, and he went away. When he returned, her father had married her to a man of Banū Asad, who had taken her away and moved with her from her people’s dwellings. Bayhas ibn Ṣuhayb then said:

poems.intro: وتوفيت "صفراء" قبل أن يدخل بها زوجها الأسدي، ولبيهس بن صهيب فيها أشعار يرثيها، وقد أوردت أخباره وأشعاره في صفراء في كتابي المترجم بكتاب "أخبار النساء" فاقتصرت على ما ذكرته ههنا من شعر، لما اقتضاه التأليف من ذكر الدمن. وقال المتنبي:

verses.h1: قف على الدمنتين بالدو من ري
verses.h2: ا، كخال في وجنة جنب خال

verses.h1: بطلول كأنهن نجوم
verses.h2: في عراص كأنهن ليالي

verses.h1: Stop at Rayyā’s two abandoned campsites in al-Daww,
verses.h2: like a mole on a cheek beside another mole.

verses.h1: At ruins that seem like stars
verses.h2: in open grounds that seem like nights.

prose_translation.intro: Ṣafrāʾ’ died before her husband, of the tribe of Asad, had consummated their marriage. Bayhas ibn Ṣuhayb composed poems lamenting her. I have included his accounts and his poems about Ṣafrāʾ’ in my book entitled Akhbār al-Nisāʾ’ (Accounts of Women), so I have confined myself here to the verses already quoted, since the plan of this compilation called for mention of abandoned campsites. Al-Mutanabbī said:

verses.h1: أراك أكبرت إدماني على الدمن
verses.h2: وحملي الشوق من باد ومكتمن

verses.h1: لا تكثرن ملامي أن عكفت على
verses.h2: ربع الحبيب فلم أعكف على وثن

verses.h1: فما وجدت على الأحشاء أوقد من
verses.h2: دمع على وطن لي في سوى وطني

verses.h1: صيرت لي من تباري عبرتي سكنا
verses.h2: مذ صرت فردا بلا إلف ولا سكن

verses.h1: I see you think my devotion to the ruins excessive,
verses.h2: and the longing I bear, both open and concealed.

verses.h1: Do not heap blame on me for keeping vigil at
verses.h2: the beloved’s dwelling: I have not kept vigil before an idol.

verses.h1: I have found nothing that sets the heart more aflame than
verses.h2: tears for a home of mine in a land not my own.

verses.h1: I made the racing of my tears a solace for myself,
verses.h2: since I became alone, without companion or dwelling.

notes.note: The phrase تباري عبرتي, literally ‘the vying of my tear(s),’ is unusual; I take it to describe tears racing one another. The unvocalized صيرت could also mean ‘you made’ rather than ‘I made.’

verses.h1: ذكر الصبي ومرابع الآرام
verses.h2: جلبت حمامي قبل وقت حمامي

verses.h1: دمن تكاثرت الهموم على في
verses.h2: عرصاتها، كتكاثر اللوام

verses.h1: وكأن كل سحابة وقفت بها
verses.h2: تبكي بعيني عروة بن حزام

verses.h1: ليس القباب على الركاب وإنما
verses.h2: هن الحياة ترحلت بسلام

verses.h1: ليت الذي خلق النوى جعل الحصى
verses.h2: لخفافهن مفاصلي وعظامي

verses.h1: Memories of youth and the gazelles’ springtime haunts
verses.h2: have brought my death before its appointed hour.

verses.h1: Ruined camps—cares crowded upon me in
verses.h2: their open grounds, as reproachers crowd.

verses.h1: As though every cloud that paused above them
verses.h2: were weeping through the eyes of ʿUrwa ibn Ḥizām.

verses.h1: Those are not canopies upon the riding camels; rather,
verses.h2: they are life itself, departing in peace.

verses.h1: Would that He who created separation had made the gravel
verses.h2: beneath their hooves out of my joints and bones.

notes.note: الصبي appears to be a misprint for الصبا, ‘youth,’ which is the reading translated here.
على appears to stand for عليّ, ‘upon me,’ which is required by the syntax and is the reading translated here.

poems.intro: وقال أبو نواس الحسن بن هانئ:

verses.h1: لمن دمن تزداد طيب نسيم
verses.h2: على طول ما أقوت وحسن رسوم

verses.h1: تجافي البلى عنهن حتى كأنما
verses.h2: لبسن على الإقواء ثوب نعيم

verses.h1: وما زال مدلولا على الربع عاشق
verses.h2: أسير لبانات، طليح هموم

verses.h1: يرى الناس أعباء على جفن عينه
verses.h2: وإن حل في وادي أخ وحميم

verses.h1: Whose are these campsite traces, ever sweeter in their breeze
verses.h2: the longer they lie deserted, and fairer in their outlines?

verses.h1: Decay has kept its distance from them, so that it is as though
verses.h2: despite their desolation, they had donned a robe of bliss.

verses.h1: And ever a lover is led to the campsite,
verses.h2: captive to longings, worn out by cares.

verses.h1: He sees people as weights upon his eyelid,
verses.h2: even if he dwells in the valley of a brother and a dear friend.

notes.note: مدلولاً على الربع is taken as ‘led to the campsite’; the precise force of this unusual expression is uncertain.

prose_translation.intro: And Abū Nuwās al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ said:

verses.h1: يا كثير النوح في الدمن
verses.h2: لا عليها بل على السكن

verses.h1: سنة العشاق واحدة
verses.h2: فإذا أحببت فاستنن

verses.h1: ظن بي من قد كلفت به
verses.h2: فهو يجفوني على الظنن

verses.h1: بات لا يعنيه ما لقيت
verses.h2: عين ممنوع من الوسن

verses.h1: رشأ لولا ملاحته
verses.h2: خلت الدنيا من الفتن

verses.h1: ما بدا إلا استرق له
verses.h2: حسنه عبدا بلا ثمن

verses.h1: O you who lament so much amid the ruins—
verses.h2: not for them, but for those who dwelt there.

verses.h1: Lovers have but one custom;
verses.h2: if you love, then follow it.

verses.h1: The one I am infatuated with suspects me,
verses.h2: and shuns me on suspicion.

verses.h1: He passed the night uncaring what had befallen
verses.h2: the eye of one denied sleep.

verses.h1: A young gazelle: were it not for his beauty,
verses.h2: the world would be free of temptation.

verses.h1: Whenever he appears, it wins him—
verses.h2: his beauty—a slave at no price.

verses.h1: أفي كل يوم منك عين ترقرق
verses.h2: وقلب على طول التذكر يخفق

verses.h1: على دمنة فيها لأدمانة النقا
verses.h2: محاسن أيام تخب وتعنق

verses.h1: وقفت فأوقفت الجوى موضع الهوى
verses.h2: ليالي عود الدهر ريان مشرق

verses.h1: فحرك بثي ربعها، وهي ساكن
verses.h2: وجدد وجدي رسمها وهو مخلق

verses.h1: Does your eye brim with tears each day,
verses.h2: and your heart throb with ceaseless remembrance,

verses.h1: over a deserted campsite where the dune’s pale gazelle
verses.h2: had lovely days that trotted and raced by?

verses.h1: I halted, and set my anguish where love had dwelt,
verses.h2: in nights when time’s bough was lush and bright.

verses.h1: Her dwelling stirred my sorrow, though it lay still;
verses.h2: its traces renewed my longing, though they were worn away.

notes.note: The source reads وهي ساكن, with a feminine pronoun that could refer to the beloved: ‘while she dwelt [there].’ The parallel contrasts favor referring instead to the motionless dwelling, as translated; وهي may be a misprint for وهو.

poems.intro: وقال ابن المولى، وهو محمد بن عبد الله بن المولى، مولى الأنصار - رضي الله عنهم -:

verses.h1: وقال خليلي
verses.h2: والبكا لي غالب أقاض على هذا البكاو التشوق؟

verses.h1: وقد طال توقافي أكفكف عبرة
verses.h2: على دمنة كادت بها النفس تزهق

verses.h1: وإنسان عيني في دوائر لجة
verses.h2: من الماء يبدو تارة ثم يغرق

verses.h1: And my friend said—
verses.h2: while weeping overwhelmed me—“Will weeping and longing be the death of this man?”

verses.h1: I had lingered long, wiping away tears
verses.h2: over a ruined campsite where my soul almost left me.

verses.h1: And the pupil of my eye, amid the eddies of a deep pool
verses.h2: of water, appears a moment, then sinks again.

notes.note: The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: والبكا لي غالب would normally complete the first hemistich. I read البكاو التشوق as البكا والتشوق, ‘weeping and longing.’ I understand أقاض على هذا as ‘will [they] be the death of this man,’ with ‘this man’ referring to the poet, though the wording is uncertain.

prose_translation.intro: And Ibn al-Mawlā—who was Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mawlā, a client of the Ansar (may God be pleased with them)—said:

poems.poet_from_text: الشيخ الأمين أبو البركات بن أبي جرادة الحلبي
poems.intro: وقال الشيخ الأمين أبو البركات بن أبي جرادة الحلبي:

poet.from_text: الشيخ الأمين أبو البركات بن أبي جرادة الحلبي

verses.h1: الناس لا هون في أماكنهم
verses.h2: ونحن في رحلة وفي ظعن

verses.h1: كأننا من متيمي العرب العر
verses.h2: باء تهوى المعاج بالدمن

verses.h1: People are carefree in their dwellings,
verses.h2: while we are journeying, on the move.

verses.h1: As though we were among the love-stricken of the pure-blooded Arabs,
verses.h2: who love to linger by the traces of abandoned camps.

notes.note: Read لا هون as لاهون, ‘carefree’ or ‘amusing themselves’; the space appears erroneous.

The subject of تهوى (‘loves’) is uncertain. The translation takes it as referring collectively to العرب (‘the Arabs’). If ‘we’ is intended, نهوى (‘we love’) would be expected. المعاج is understood as stopping or lingering.

prose_translation.intro: And the trustworthy shaykh Abū al-Barakāt ibn Abī Jarāda al-Ḥalabī said:

poems.intro: هذان البيتان للشيخ الأمين أبي البركات بن أبي جرادة، وكان أمينا على خزانة الملك العادل نور الدين، فكان لا يزال معه في سفر، ولم يكن معتادا لذلك، فتبرم بما هو فيه من الحركة والسفر المستمر في الأخطار والحروب، فكتب إلى أخيه ثقة الملك أبي عبد الله - رحمهما الله - أبياتا، منها البيتان المقدمة، وأنا ذاكر القطعة بكمالها:

verses.h1: يا ثقتي أنت مشتكى حزني
verses.h2: قد فاتني كل مطلب حسن

verses.h1: ما قصرت همتي فأجعلها
verses.h2: مظنة الإتهام والظنن

verses.h1: أملت أن أقتنى من المجد
verses.h2: والسؤدد ما لا يباع بالثمن

verses.h1: واقتفى سنة الألى درجوا
verses.h2: قبلي على واضح من السنن

verses.h1: راغب نفس فيما يزهدني
verses.h2: ناعم بال بعيشي الخشن

verses.h1: حيث لا أبتغي مزاحمة الخل
verses.h2: ق ولا أشرئب للمنن

verses.h1: ولا يراني امرؤ ألوذ به
verses.h2: إلا خليلي في الله أو سكني

verses.h1: هذا الذي رمته فعارضني
verses.h2: في كونه عارض من الزمن

verses.h1: أصبح شملي إلى الشتات وأص
verses.h2: بحت غريبا، وما نبا وطني

verses.h1: ولا جفاني أهل الصفاء ولا
verses.h2: شربت در الصفاء بالضفن

verses.h1: الناس لا هون في أماكنهم
verses.h2: ونحن في رحلة وفي ظعن

verses.h1: كأننا من متيمي العرب العر
verses.h2: باء تهوى المعاج بالدمن

verses.h1: لا صبر لي قد خرجت من جلدي
verses.h2: وقد سلبت الحصين من جنني

verses.h1: وأسخن اليأس ناظري فما
verses.h2: يقر للمطمعات في الرسن

verses.h1: ومج سمعي لغو الحديث فما
verses.h2: يطور شيء منه على أذني

verses.h1: وعدت من كل ما أومله
verses.h2: أوقل: حسبي بصحة البدن

verses.h1: أي عرى حالة علقت بها
verses.h2: وأي شتى قرنت في قرن

verses.h1: جمعت
verses.h2: والهفتاه قلب فتى يفتر عن هم شارخ يفن

verses.h1: ورتبة في العلاء تتبعها
verses.h2: صورة مستبذل وممتهن

verses.h1: مت ونفسي على باقية
verses.h2: وضعت والحافظات تحفظني

verses.h1: واخيبة الحاسدين كم منح
verses.h2: مغبوطة، وهي أعظم المحن!

verses.h1: يا ليت أني قبل المنية قد
verses.h2: غببت في حفرتي وفي كفني

verses.h1: يا ليت ما كان من حياتي
verses.h2: إذ ال أمر على ما أراه لم يكن!

verses.h1: O my trusted one, to you I bring my grief:
verses.h2: every worthy goal has eluded me.

verses.h1: My ambition has not fallen short, that I should make it
verses.h2: a target of accusation and suspicion.

verses.h1: I hoped to acquire such glory
verses.h2: and eminence as no price could buy,

verses.h1: and follow the way of those who passed
verses.h2: before me along a clear path:

verses.h1: eager at heart for what fosters renunciation,
verses.h2: content in my rough way of life,

verses.h1: where I seek no rivalry
verses.h2: with others, nor crane my neck for favors.

verses.h1: No man sees me seeking refuge with him
verses.h2: save my friend in God or one who gives me peace.

verses.h1: That is what I sought, but I was thwarted
verses.h2: in its fulfillment by a setback of fortune.

verses.h1: All that held my life together has scattered,
verses.h2: and I have become a stranger, though my homeland has not rejected me.

verses.h1: Nor have my faithful friends shunned me, nor
verses.h2: have I drunk the milk of affection mixed with rancor.

verses.h1: People live at leisure in their own places,
verses.h2: while we are ever journeying and on the move.

verses.h1: As though we were among the love-stricken Arabs—
verses.h2: Arabs of pure stock, longing to stop at abandoned camps.

verses.h1: I have no patience left: I have burst out of my skin,
verses.h2: and been stripped of the stoutest of my shields.

verses.h1: Despair has made my eye burn,
verses.h2: and it will not stay reined in by tempting hopes.

verses.h1: My hearing has spat out idle talk,
verses.h2: and none of it comes near my ear.

verses.h1: From all that I hoped for I have come back
verses.h2: saying: “Bodily health is enough for me.”

verses.h1: What bonds of circumstance have I fastened on,
verses.h2: and what disparate things have I bound in one yoke!

verses.h1: I have joined together
verses.h2: —alas!—a young man’s heart that reveals the cares of one both youthful and aged,

verses.h1: and a lofty rank, attended by
verses.h2: the outward appearance of a drudge held in contempt.

verses.h1: I have died, though my soul remains within me;
verses.h2: I have been brought low, though the guardians guard me.

verses.h1: What disappointment for the envious! How many gifts
verses.h2: are envied, yet are the greatest afflictions!

verses.h1: Would that, before death, I had already
verses.h2: been hidden away in my grave and my shroud!

verses.h1: Would that all the life I have lived—
verses.h2: since things are as I see them—had never been!

notes.note: The precise sense of فيما يزهدني is uncertain. Literally it suggests “in what makes me renounce,” without specifying what is renounced; the translation takes it as referring to an austere, independent life.
بالضفن is unclear in this context. The translation conjecturally reads بالضغن, “with rancor,” giving affection’s milk mixed with resentment.
لا هون is read as لاهون, “at leisure” or “amusing themselves,” with an erroneous space.
The grammatical attachment of تهوى, “loves/desires,” is uncertain; it may refer collectively to العرب. المعاج is understood as turning aside or stopping at the abandoned camps.
أوقل appears to be a transposition error for أقول, “I say.”

The supplied hemistich division appears misplaced: the likely division is after قلب فتى rather than after جمعت. It has been preserved as supplied. The phrase هم شارخ يفن is also difficult: شارخ denotes someone youthful, while يفن denotes a decrepit old man. The translation tentatively takes هم as “cares” and retains the apparent contradiction.

ونفسي على باقية is problematic; على may represent عليّ, but the construction remains uncertain. The translation gives the probable contrast between being dead and still having one’s soul. وضعت is read as “I was brought low.” The identity of الحافظات, “the guardians,” is unclear.
غببت appears to be a typing or OCR error for غُيِّبت, “I was hidden away,” which is followed in the translation.
إذ ال أمر appears to have faulty spacing or lettering. The translation reads إذ الأمر, “since the situation,” though إذ آل أمر, “since matters have come to,” may also have been intended.

prose_translation.intro: These two verses are by the shaykh al-Amīn Abū al-Barakāt ibn Abī Jarāda, who was entrusted with the treasury of al-Malik al-ʿĀdil Nūr al-Dīn and was therefore constantly accompanying him on his journeys. He was not accustomed to this, and grew weary of the restless movement and continual travel amid dangers and wars. He therefore wrote some verses to his brother, Thiqat al-Mulk Abū ʿAbd Allah—may God have mercy on them both—including the two verses given above. I shall now quote the piece in full:

opening.actual: ألا يا غرابي دمنة الدار بيننا

verses.h1: ألا يا غرابي دمنة الدار بيننا
verses.h2: أبا لهجر من عفراء تنتجيان؟

verses.h1: فإن كان حقا ما تقولان فانهضا
verses.h2: بحلمي إلى وكريكما فكلاني

verses.h1: فعفراء أصفى الناس عندي مودة
verses.h2: وعفراء عني المعرض المتواني

verses.h1: فوالله ما حدثت سرك صاحبا
verses.h2: نصيحا، ولا فاهت به الشفتان

verses.h1: سوى أنني قد قلت يوما لصاحبي
verses.h2: ضحى، وقلوصانا بنا تخدان

verses.h1: ألا حبذا من حب عفراء ملتقى
verses.h2: نعام، وبرك، حيث يلتقيان

verses.h1: O you two ravens on the dwelling’s traces between us,
verses.h2: are you whispering together of parting from ʿAfrāʾ?

verses.h1: If what you say is true, then fly away
verses.h2: with my flesh to your two nests, and eat me.

verses.h1: For ʿAfrāʾ, above all others, has my purest affection,
verses.h2: yet ʿAfrāʾ turns away from me and holds back.

verses.h1: By God, I have not told your secret to a friend,
verses.h2: however faithful, nor have my lips uttered it—

verses.h1: save that I once said to my companion
verses.h2: one forenoon, as our two she-camels bore us swiftly along:

verses.h1: “Ah, for love of ʿAfrāʾ, how dear is the confluence
verses.h2: of Naʿām and Birk, where the two meet!”

notes.note: أبا لهجر appears to be a spacing error for أبالهجر, ‘is it of parting …?’
بحلمي (‘with my forbearance’ or ‘with my understanding’) appears corrupted. The translation assumes بلحمي, ‘with my flesh,’ which fits the ravens’ eating him.
The first hemistich is ambiguous: it may instead describe ʿAfrāʾ as the sincerest of people in her affection, in the speaker’s estimation.
Naʿām and Birk appear to be two valleys. The vocalization of برك, rendered here as Birk, is uncertain.

verses.h1: لمن دمنة بالنعف عاف صعيدها
verses.h2: تغير باقيها ومح جديدها

verses.h1: لسعدة في عام الهريمة إذ بنا
verses.h2: تصاف، وإذ لما يرعنا صدودها

verses.h1: وإذ هي أما نفسها فأريبة
verses.h2: للهو، وأما عن صبي فتذودها

verses.h1: تصيد ألباب الرجال بدلها
verses.h2: وشيمتها وحشية لا نصيدها

verses.h1: كباسقة الوسمي ساعة أسبلت
verses.h2: تلألأ فيها البرق وابيض جيدها

verses.h1: Whose camp-trace is this at al-Naʿf, its ground effaced,
verses.h2: its remnants altered, its freshness worn away?

verses.h1: Saʿda’s, from the year of al-Hurayma, when between us
verses.h2: there was affection, and her turning away had not yet distressed us.

verses.h1: And when she herself was skilled
verses.h2: in dalliance, yet kept herself from passion.

verses.h1: She snares men’s hearts with her coquetry,
verses.h2: but her nature is untamed—we cannot snare her.

verses.h1: Like a towering cloud of the autumn rains as it lets down its showers,
verses.h2: lightning flashing within it, its neck gleaming white.

notes.note: Al-Naʿf may be a place name or a descriptive term for sloping ground beside a mountain or valley.
I could not identify the event or period called ‘the year of al-Hurayma’; the vocalization of الهريمة is uncertain.

The reading صبي is unclear. ‘Passion’ provisionally takes it as a form of ṣibā, youthful infatuation or folly, possibly with a final-letter error. The pronoun in فتذودها is taken to refer back to نفسها: she restrains herself.

poems.intro: وقال الشريف المرتضى رضي الله عنه:

verses.h1: فإما شئتما أن تسعداني
verses.h2: فمرا بين على الدمن البوالي

verses.h1: خرسن، فلو ملكن النطق يوما
verses.h2: شكون إليك من جنف الليالي

verses.h1: If you two wish to console me,
verses.h2: then take me past the weathered ruins.

verses.h1: They are mute; if ever they could speak,
verses.h2: they would complain to you of the nights’ injustice.

notes.note: بين in the second hemistich appears to be a misprint for بي: فمرا بي, “take me past.” The translation follows this reading.

prose_translation.intro: Al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā, may God be pleased with him, said:

verses.h1: فيا دمنة الحي الذين تحملوا
verses.h2: بوادي الغضى ماذا ألم بنا منك؟

verses.h1: خشعت فلا عين تراك لناظر
verses.h2: دثورا، ولا نطق يخبرنا عنك

verses.h1: وأذكرها والشيب يضحك ثغره
verses.h2: بلماتنا عهد الشبيبة والفتك

verses.h1: ليالي لا حلم لذي الحلم والنهى
verses.h2: هناك، ولا نسك يصاب لذي نسك

verses.h1: O campsite of the tribe who departed,
verses.h2: in Wādī al-Ghaḍā—what have we suffered because of you!

verses.h1: You have sunk low: no beholder’s eye can see you,
verses.h2: so effaced you are, nor does any voice tell us of you.

verses.h1: And I remember it—while gray hair flashes its smiling teeth
verses.h2: amid our locks—the days of youth and reckless daring.

verses.h1: Nights when the forbearing and wise had no restraint
verses.h2: there, nor could piety be found in the pious.

notes.note: The grammatical connection of «عهد الشبيبة والفتك» (‘the days of youth and reckless daring’) to «أذكرها» (‘I remember it’) is compressed and somewhat ambiguous. I take it as specifying the days recalled in connection with the campsite.

verses.h1: لمن دمنة أقفرت بالجناب
verses.h2: إلى السفح بين الملا فالهضاب

verses.h1: بكيت لعرفان آياتها
verses.h2: وهاج لك الشوق نعب الغراب

verses.h1: Whose campsite lies desolate at al-Janāb,
verses.h2: extending to the slope, between al-Malā and the hills?

verses.h1: You wept on recognizing its traces,
verses.h2: and the raven’s croak stirred longing in you.

notes.note: Al-Janāb and al-Malā are treated as place names; their precise locations here are uncertain. Al-safḥ, translated as ‘the slope,’ may also be a place name.
The unvocalized بكيت could mean ‘I wept’ or ‘you wept’; the latter is adopted to match the following ‘in you’ (لك).

verses.h1: دمن إذا اشتثبت عينك عهدها
verses.h2: رجعت إليك بنظرة المتوسم

verses.h1: فتكت بها سنتان يعتورانها
verses.h2: بالعاصفات وكل أسحم مرزم

verses.h1: Ruins—when you ask your eye to confirm its memory of them,
verses.h2: it returns to you with the gaze of one searching for signs.

verses.h1: Two years have ravaged them, assailing them in turn
verses.h2: with violent winds and every dark, thundering cloud.

notes.note: اشتثبت appears to be a misprint for استثبت. I understand the phrase as asking the eye to confirm its recollection of the ruins, though the syntax of عينك عهدها is uncertain.

prose_translation.intro: And Ashjaʿ ibn ʿAmr al-Sulamī said:

verses.h1: رحلوا بأيامي الرقاق على
verses.h2: آثارهم، وبعيشي السهل

verses.h1: وعكفت بعدهم على ضمن
verses.h2: عرف البلى فبلى كما يبلى

verses.h1: جسدي، ودمنته بما نحلا
verses.h2: يتشاكيان تصدع الشمل

verses.h1: مغنى وضعنا أمس من شعف
verses.h2: سافي ثراه مواضع الكحل

verses.h1: They departed, taking my tender days
verses.h2: in their wake, and my life of ease.

verses.h1: I lingered after them beside an ailing remnant,
verses.h2: which knew decay and wasted as things waste.

verses.h1: My body and the ruined dwelling, both wasted away,
verses.h2: lament to each other the scattering of our company.

verses.h1: A dwelling where yesterday, out of passionate love, we laid
verses.h2: its windblown dust upon our eyes like kohl.

notes.note: ضمن is uncertain. I tentatively read it as ضَمِن, ‘ailing,’ describing the abandoned dwelling figuratively; it may instead be a textual error.

The syntax of فبلى كما يبلى is unclear. The following جسدي (‘my body’) may supply the subject of يبلى, giving ‘wasted as my body wastes,’ but it also appears to begin the paired subject ‘my body and the ruined dwelling’ in line 3.

verses.h1: عفا رسم برامة فالتلاع
verses.h2: فكثبان الحضير إلى لفاع

verses.h1: عفاها كل هطال سكوب
verses.h2: يشبه صوته صوت اليراع

verses.h1: وقفت بها أسائلها طويلا
verses.h2: وما فيها مجاوبة لداع

verses.h1: تحمل أهلها منها فبانوا
verses.h2: فأبكتني المنازل للرواع

interludes.text: (اليراع: القصب التي يصفر بها، ويروى صوت الرباع يقال: ربع ورباع وهو ولد الناقة إذا كان له عشرة أيام) .

verses.h1: The traces at Rāmah have faded, and in the ravines,
verses.h2: and on the dunes of al-Ḥuḍayr as far as Lifāʿ.

verses.h1: Every cloud pouring torrents has effaced them,
verses.h2: its sound resembling the sound of reed pipes.

verses.h1: I stood there questioning them at length,
verses.h2: but there was none there to answer a caller.

verses.h1: Their people packed up and departed from them,
verses.h2: and the dwellings made me weep in dismay.

notes.note: The places الحضير and لفاع are not securely identified; the vocalizations al-Ḥuḍayr and Lifāʿ are tentative. التلاع is taken as the common noun ‘ravines,’ though it could be a place name.
للرواع is obscure here and may be corrupt. ‘In dismay’ tentatively connects it with روع, ‘fright’; the intended sense is uncertain.

interludes: (Al-yarāʿ: reeds used as pipes for whistling. Another reading is “the sound of camel calves” (ṣawt al-rubāʿ). One says rubaʿ and rubāʿ of a she-camel’s young when it is ten days old.)

verses.h1: أشاقتك بالنقع الغداة رسوم
verses.h2: دوارس أدنى عهدهن قديم

verses.h1: دوارس أما أهلها فتحملوا
verses.h2: فبانوا، وأما خيمها فمقيم

verses.h1: وما ذاك إلا من جميع تفرقت
verses.h2: بهم نية بعد الجوار قسم

verses.h1: فعادوا كبرد العصب شق فأصبحوا
verses.h2: فمحتمل غاد، وظل مقيم

verses.h1: وذلك دأب للنوى ليس مخلفي
verses.h2: إذا كان لي جار علي كريم

verses.h1: Did the traces at al-Naqʿ stir your longing this morning—
verses.h2: effaced, their last days of habitation long ago?

verses.h1: Effaced: their people have packed up
verses.h2: and gone away, while their tent frames remain.

verses.h1: These are but traces of a company once united,
verses.h2: scattered by their destinations after living side by side.

verses.h1: They became like a striped cloak torn apart:
verses.h2: one packing up and leaving at dawn, another staying behind.

verses.h1: Such is separation’s way—it never fails me
verses.h2: whenever I have a neighbor dear to me.

notes.note: Al-Naqʿ is taken as a place-name; its location is uncertain. أدنى عهدهن may refer to the most recent habitation of the sites or the speaker’s last acquaintance with them.
خيم can denote tents or their wooden frameworks; the latter sense is used here.

The final word قسم is unclear and may be corrupted; as printed, it also appears inconsistent with the other rhyme endings. The translation follows the apparent overall sense, taking نية as the destination or direction of departure.
وظل مقيم is read as ‘and another remained.’ Without vocalization, ظل could instead be the noun ‘shade,’ yielding ‘a lingering shade.’

prose_translation.intro: And Muzāḥim ibn al-Ḥārith al-ʿUqaylī said:

verses.h1: أما الرسوم فقد أذكرن ما سلفا
verses.h2: فلا تكفن عن شأنيك أن يقفا

verses.h1: لا عذر للصب أن يقنى السلو، ولا
verses.h2: للدمع بعد مضي الحي أن يقفا

verses.h1: حتى يظل بماء سافح ودم
verses.h2: في الربع يحسب من عينيه قد رعفا

verses.h1: As for the traces, they have recalled what is past;
verses.h2: so do not let your two tear ducts cease to flow.

verses.h1: The lovesick man has no excuse for finding solace, nor
verses.h2: have tears any excuse for stopping after the tribe has gone,

verses.h1: until he remains amid streaming tears and blood,
verses.h2: at the campsite, seemingly bleeding from his eyes.

notes.note: شأنيك is understood as ‘your two tear ducts.’ The construction فلا تكفن عن شأنيك أن يقفا is unclear and may be corrupt; the translation follows the apparent injunction to continue weeping.

opening.actual: ألا لا أرى مثلي امترى اليوم

verses.h1: ألا لا أرى مثلي امترى اليوم في رسم
verses.h2: تغص به عيني ويلفظه وهمي

verses.h1: أنت صور الأشياء بيني وبينه
verses.h2: فجهلي كلا جهل، وعلمي كلا علم

verses.h1: Ah, I see none like me, doubting today over a dwelling’s trace:
verses.h2: My eye chokes on it, and my imagination spits it out.

verses.h1: The forms of things have come between me and it,
verses.h2: So my ignorance is no true ignorance, and my knowledge no true knowledge.

notes.note: The opening أنت is unclear as printed and may be corrupt. The translation tentatively reads أتت, ‘have come’; this emendation is uncertain.

poems.poet_from_text: أبو عبد الله بن الخياط الدمشقي
poems.intro: وقال أبو عبد الله بن الخياط الدمشقي:

opening.actual: هو الرسم لو أغنى الوقوف على

poet.from_text: أبو عبد الله بن الخياط الدمشقي

verses.h1: هو الرسم لو أغنى الوقوف على الرسم
verses.h2: هو الحزم لولا بعد عهدك بالحزم

verses.h1: عشية جن القلب فيها جنونه
verses.h2: ونازعني شوقي منازعة الخصم

verses.h1: فلما أبى إلا البكاء على الأسى
verses.h2: بكيت فما أبقيت للرسم من رسم

verses.h1: لقد وجدت وجدي الديار بأهلها
verses.h2: ولو لم تجد وجدي لما سقمت سقمي

verses.h1: منازل أدراس شجاني نحولها
verses.h2: فهلا شجاها ناحل القلب والجسم؟

verses.h1: سقاها الحيا قبلي فلما سقيتها
verses.h2: دموي رأت فضل الولي على الوسمي

verses.h1: Here are the traces—if standing over traces could avail;
verses.h2: that is prudence—were you not so long estranged from prudence.

verses.h1: That evening, the heart went utterly mad,
verses.h2: and my longing contended with me like an adversary.

verses.h1: When it would accept nothing but weeping in sorrow,
verses.h2: I wept until I left not a trace of those remains.

verses.h1: The dwellings felt my longing for their people;
verses.h2: had they not felt my longing, they would not have sickened as I did.

verses.h1: Effaced dwellings, whose wasting grieved me—
verses.h2: why did one wasted in heart and body not grieve them?

verses.h1: Rain watered them before me; then, when I watered them
verses.h2: with my tears, they saw how the later rain surpassed the first autumn showers.

notes.note: The referent of هو in هو الحزم (‘that is prudence’) is unclear; it may refer to standing at the traces.
The subject of أبى (‘would accept nothing’) could be either the heart or the speaker’s longing.
دموي appears to be a misprint for دموعي (‘my tears’), which is the reading translated here.

prose_translation.intro: And Abū ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Khayyāṭ al-Dimashqī said:

verses.h1: أفي رسم دار دمعك المتحدر
verses.h2: سفاها، وما استنطاق ما ليس يخبر

verses.h1: تغير ذاك الرسم من بعد جدة
verses.h2: وكل جديد مرة يتغير

verses.h1: Is it over the traces of a dwelling that your tears stream,
verses.h2: in folly? What use is questioning what cannot answer?

verses.h1: Those traces have changed since they were fresh,
verses.h2: and everything new changes in time.

verses.h1: أرسوم دار أم سطور كتاب
verses.h2: درست بشاشتها مع الأحقاب

verses.h1: يجتاز زائرها بغير لبانة
verses.h2: ويرد سائلها بغير جواب

verses.h1: ولربما كان الزمان محببا
verses.h2: فينا بمن فيها من الأحباب

verses.h1: Are these the traces of a dwelling, or lines in a book,
verses.h2: their freshness faded with the passing ages?

verses.h1: Its visitor passes on with his wish unfulfilled,
verses.h2: and its questioner is turned away without an answer.

verses.h1: How often time was made dear
verses.h2: to us by the loved ones who dwelt there.

poems.intro: وقال زهير بن أبي سلمى المزني:

verses.h1: هاج الفؤاد معارف الرسم
verses.h2: قفرا بذي الهضبات كالوشم

verses.h1: ولقد أراها والحلول بها
verses.h2: من بعد صرم أيما صرم

verses.h1: فاستأثر الدهر الغداة بهم
verses.h2: والدهر يرميني ولا أرمي

verses.h1: لو كان لي قرنا أناضله
verses.h2: ما طاش عند حفيظة سهمي

verses.h1: أو كان يعطي النصف قلت له
verses.h2: أحرزت قسمك فاله عن قسمي

verses.h1: The campsite’s familiar traces stirred my heart,
verses.h2: desolate at Dhū al-Haḍabāt, like a tattoo.

verses.h1: I used to see it with its people dwelling there,
verses.h2: band after band—what fine bands they were!

verses.h1: But this morning Time claimed them for itself;
verses.h2: Time shoots at me, and I do not shoot back.

verses.h1: Were it an adversary I could match in archery,
verses.h2: my arrow would not stray when my anger rose.

verses.h1: Or if it would deal fairly, I would tell it:
verses.h2: “You have secured your share; leave mine alone.”

notes.note: Dhū al-Haḍabāt appears to be a place-name; its location is uncertain.
The syntax of “من بعد صرم أيما صرم” is uncertain. The translation takes ṣirm as a band of people and understands the phrase as praising successive groups of inhabitants.

prose_translation.intro: And Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā al-Muzanī said:

verses.h1: خليلي عوجا منكما اليوم أو دعا
verses.h2: نحيي رسوما بالقبيبة بلقعا

verses.h1: أربت بها الأرواح حتى تنسفت
verses.h2: معارفها إلا الصفيح الموضعا

verses.h1: وغير ثلاث في الديار كأنها
verses.h2: ثلاث حمامات تقابلن وقعا

verses.h1: بكيت عيني اليسرى فلما زجرتها عن الجهل بعد الحلم أسبلتا معا
My two friends, turn aside today—or leave it be—
verses.h2: let us greet the desolate traces at al-Qubayba.

verses.h1: The winds persisted there until they swept away
verses.h2: its recognizable features, save the flat stones laid in place,

verses.h1: And three stones in the dwellings, as though they were
verses.h2: three doves perched facing one another.

verses.h1: My left eye wept; when I rebuked it for folly after forbearance, both eyes streamed together.

notes.note: The object of أو دعا, literally ‘or leave [it],’ is unstated; the precise force of this alternative is uncertain.
The noun following ‘three’ is omitted; hearthstones are presumably intended.
بكيت appears to be a misprint for بكت, ‘wept,’ which is the reading translated. As written, it could alternatively be vocalized بكّيت, ‘I made [my eye] weep.’

poems.intro: (كان الصمة أعور، فيقول: إنه بكى بعينه الصحيحة، فلما زجرها، أي كفكفها فاضت العين التالفة) . وقال جرير بن عطية:

verses.h1: أقول لصحبتي لما ارتحلنا
verses.h2: ودمع العين منهمر سجام

verses.h1: أتمضون الرسوم ولا تحيا
verses.h2: كلامكم علي إذن حرام

verses.h1: مقام الحي مر له ثمان
verses.h2: إلى عشرين قد بلى المقام

verses.h1: I say to my companions as we depart,
verses.h2: while tears stream and pour from my eyes:

verses.h1: Do you pass the ruins without greeting them?
verses.h2: Then speaking with you is forbidden to me.

verses.h1: The tribe’s camping ground—eight years have passed over it,
verses.h2: added to twenty; the camping ground has worn away.

prose_translation.intro: (Al-Ṣimma was blind in one eye. He says that he wept with his sound eye, but when he checked it—that is, stemmed its tears—the damaged eye overflowed.) And Jarīr ibn ʿAṭiyya said:

poems.intro: تعالى فوق أجرعك الخزامي ... بنور، واستهل بك الغمام وقال البحتري:

verses.h1: ما على الركب من وقوف الركاب
verses.h2: في مغاني الصبى ورسم التصابي

verses.h1: أين أهل القباب بالأجزع الفر
verses.h2: د، تولوا، لا أين أهل القباب!

verses.h1: عرجوا فالدموع إن أبك في الرسم
verses.h2: ، دموعي والاكتئاب اكتئابي

verses.h1: وكمثل الأحباب لو يعلم العا
verses.h2: ذل عندي منازل الأحباب

verses.h1: What harm to the riders if their mounts halt
verses.h2: in the haunts of youth and the traces of youthful love?

verses.h1: Where are the people of the tents at al-Ajzaʿ al-Fard?
verses.h2: They have departed—oh, where are the people of the tents!

verses.h1: Turn aside: if I weep among the traces, the tears
verses.h2: are mine, and the sorrow is mine.

verses.h1: Like my loved ones—if the reproacher only knew—
verses.h2: are the dwellings of my loved ones to me.

notes.note: Al-Ajzaʿ al-Fard is unidentified; it may be a descriptive expression rather than a place name. The spelling الأجزع may also be a misprint for الأجرع, a sandy tract. The word al-Fard is divided between the source hemistichs.
The wording لا أين is syntactically unusual and possibly corrupt. It is provisionally rendered as an emphatic repetition of the question: ‘oh, where ...!’

prose_translation.intro:
May lavender rise in bloom upon your sandy knoll, and may the clouds pour rain upon you.

Al-Buḥturī said:

poems.intro: وقال عمر بن أبي ربيعة المخزومي:

verses.h1: أمن رسم دار دمعك المترقرق
verses.h2: سفاها، وما استنطاق ما ليس ينطق

verses.h1: بحيث التقى جمع ومفضى محسر
verses.h2: معالمه كادت على العهد تخلق

verses.h1: ذكرت بها ما قدمضى وتذكر ال
verses.h2: حبيب، ورسم الدار مما يشوق

verses.h1: ليالي من دهر إذ الحي حيرة
verses.h2: وإذ هو مأهول الخميلة مونق

verses.h1: Is it for the traces of a dwelling that your tears well up
verses.h2: in folly? What use is questioning what cannot speak?

verses.h1: Where Jamʿ meets the outlet of Muḥassir,
verses.h2: its landmarks have nearly worn away with time.

verses.h1: There I recalled what had passed; remembering
verses.h2: the beloved and the traces of home awakens longing.

verses.h1: Nights long ago, when the tribe were neighbors,
verses.h2: when its grove was peopled and the place was lovely.

notes.note: The printed ‘قدمضى’ is read as ‘قد مضى’ (‘had passed’).
‘حيرة’ is unclear here. The translation tentatively reads it as ‘جيرة’ (‘neighbors’), a plausible copying or OCR error.

prose_translation.intro: And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī said:

poems.intro: وقال كثير بن عبد الرحمن الخزاعي:

verses.h1: أمن آل سلمى الرسم أنت مسائل
verses.h2: نعم، والمغاني قد درسن مواثل

verses.h1: فظلت بها تفضي على حد عبرة
verses.h2: كأنك من تجريبك الدهر جاهل

verses.h1: وقد كان ما فيه لذي اللب عبرة
verses.h2: ورأى لذي رأي، فهل أنت عاقل؟

verses.h1: تذكر إخوان مضوا فتتابعوا
verses.h2: وشيب علا منك المفارق شامل

verses.h1: Is it the trace of Salmā’s folk that you question?
verses.h2: Yes—the dwelling sites have faded, though still visible.

verses.h1: So you lingered there, on the verge of tears,
verses.h2: as though, for all your experience of time, you knew nothing.

verses.h1: Yet what time holds has offered a lesson to anyone with understanding,
verses.h2: and counsel to anyone with judgment—will you understand?

verses.h1: You remember brothers who departed, following one another,
verses.h2: while gray hair has spread over all the partings of your hair.

notes.note: The expression تفضي على حد عبرة is unclear, particularly the verb تفضي in this construction. “On the verge of tears” is a tentative rendering; the verb may be misprinted.
I read ورأى as ورأي, “and counsel/judgment,” parallel to عبرة, “a lesson.” The printed form appears to be a spelling or transcription error.

prose_translation.intro: And Kuthayyir ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Khuzāʿī said:

verses.h1: أهاجتك أطلال الرسوم الدوائر
verses.h2: بأدعاص حوضي المغنقات النوادر

verses.h1: نعم هاجت الأطلال شوقا كفى به
verses.h2: من الشوق إلا أنه غير ظاهر

verses.h1: فما زلت أطوى النفس حتى كأنها
verses.h2: بذي الرمث لم تخطر على بال خاطر

verses.h1: حياء وإشفاقا من الركب أن يروا
verses.h2: دليلا على مستودعات الضمائر

verses.h1: Have the worn-away traces of the encampments stirred you
verses.h2: by the high, jutting sandhills of Ḥawḍā?

verses.h1: Yes, the ruins stirred a longing—enough indeed
verses.h2: of longing, though it does not show.

verses.h1: I kept concealing my feelings, until it was as though
verses.h2: at Dhū al-Ramth they had never crossed anyone’s mind,

verses.h1: out of shame and fear that my fellow riders might see
verses.h2: some sign of the secrets stored within the heart.

notes.note: المغنقات is unclear and may be a misprint for المعنقات, describing something rising high or projecting; ‘high’ follows that conjecture. النوادر is taken to describe projecting or isolated dunes. حوضي is read as the place-name Ḥawḍā (حوضى).

The feminine pronoun in كأنها has an uncertain referent. The translation takes it to refer to النفس, understood here as the speaker’s inward feelings; a reference to an unmentioned beloved is also possible. Dhū al-Ramth is treated as a place-name, but its location is unidentified.

verses.h1: ورب رسم ماثل
verses.h2: أعجم ثم بينا

verses.h1: وقال: من هنا طع
verses.h2: ن، وغربن من هنا

verses.h1: يا بأبي المسكون لو
verses.h2: أني وجدت السكنا

verses.h1: قالوا: النوى تسمية
verses.h2: والموت يعني من عنى

verses.h1: من اشتكى أشجانه
verses.h2: فما أحس الشجنا

verses.h1: كان فؤادي وهم
verses.h2: فظعنوا وظعنا

verses.h1: لم يترك الغادون لي
verses.h2: قلبا نجن الحزنا

verses.h1: Many a trace of a dwelling, still visible,
verses.h2: was mute, then spoke clearly.

verses.h1: It said, “From here they journeyed,
verses.h2: and from here they went west.”

verses.h1: My father be ransom for that dwelling—if only
verses.h2: I could find those who dwelt there!

verses.h1: They said, “Parting is only a name;
verses.h2: whoever speaks of it means death.”

verses.h1: Whoever complains of his sorrows
verses.h2: has not felt sorrow.

verses.h1: My heart and they were together;
verses.h2: they departed, and it departed too.

verses.h1: Those who left at dawn left me
verses.h2: no heart to harbor sorrow.

notes.note: طعن, divided between the hemistichs, is taken in the sense of journeying. It may instead be a misprint for ظعن, “departed.”
The syntax of والموت يعني من عنى is compressed and ambiguous. The translation takes الموت as the fronted object: whoever means “parting” really means death.
نجن appears corrupt. The translation tentatively reads يجن, “conceals” or “harbors,” with “heart” as its subject.

verses.h1: ما بال رسم بكثيب الحمى
verses.h2: عطلا بلا شاء ولا جامل

verses.h1: حالت مغانيه ووجدي به
verses.h2: غض جديد ليس بالحائل

verses.h1: لو أبصرتني ناحلا عينه
verses.h2: لاستأنس الناحل بالناحل

verses.h1: Why do the campsite’s remains at the dune of al-Ḥimā
verses.h2: lie deserted, with neither sheep nor a herd of camels?

verses.h1: Its dwellings have changed, yet my longing for it
verses.h2: is tender and fresh, unchanged.

verses.h1: If its eye could see me wasted away,
verses.h2: one wasted form would find solace in another.

prose_translation.intro: And al-Murtaḍā—may God be pleased with him—said:

poems.poet: عبد العزيز بن الحسين القاضي الجليس
poems.poet_from_text: القاضي الجليس أبو المعالي عبد العزيز بن الحسين
poems.intro: وقال القاضي الجليس أبو المعالي عبد العزيز بن الحسين، المعروف بابن الحباب:

poet.expected: عبد العزيز بن الحسين القاضي الجليس
poet.from_text: القاضي الجليس أبو المعالي عبد العزيز بن الحسين

verses.h1: أجدك لا تراك العين تذرى
verses.h2: عقيقا كلما لاح العقيق

verses.h1: سقى رمل الحمى ورسوم مغنى ال
verses.h2: لوى هزج يروق بما يريق

verses.h1: فيكسو عاطل الهضبات روضا
verses.h2: له من زهره حلى أنيق

verses.h1: أراق الطل مدمعه عليه
verses.h2: وشق جيوبه فيه الشقيق

verses.h1: Can it be that the eye does not see you shedding
verses.h2: carnelian whenever al-ʿAqīq comes into view?

verses.h1: May the sands of al-Ḥimā and the traces of the abode at
verses.h2: al-Liwā be watered by a thundering cloud, delighting with what it pours.

verses.h1: And may it clothe the bare hills in a meadow
verses.h2: whose flowers form its lovely ornaments.

verses.h1: The dew has poured its tears upon it,
verses.h2: and the anemones have torn their robes at the breast there.

notes.note: The precise place intended by al-ʿAqīq is uncertain.
The locations intended by al-Ḥimā and al-Liwā are uncertain. Al-Ḥimā may instead mean simply ‘the protected pasture.’

prose_translation.intro: And the judge al-Jalīs Abū al-Maʿālī ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Ḥusayn, known as Ibn al-Ḥabbāb, said:

verses.h1: وقفت على رسم ببيداء بلقع
verses.h2: خلي من النادي صموت إذا دعي

verses.h1: نبت عنه عيني ثم قال لها البلى
verses.h2: : هي الدار فاذرى من دموعك أو دعي

verses.h1: ولا تنكرن للدهر إخلاق جدة
verses.h2: وتشتيت آلاف وإيحاش مجمع

verses.h1: فللموت سكان الديار، وللبلى
verses.h2: منازلهم، وشملهم للتصدع

verses.h1: فصبرا فإن رد التفجع والأسى
verses.h2: عليك الذي ولى من الأمر فاجزع

verses.h1: I stood by the traces of a dwelling in a barren wilderness,
verses.h2: empty of company, silent when called upon.

verses.h1: My eye turned away from it; then decay said to my eye:
verses.h2: “This is the dwelling: shed your tears, or refrain.”

verses.h1: Do not think it strange that time wears out what is new,
verses.h2: scatters companions, and leaves a gathering place desolate.

verses.h1: For the inhabitants of homes belong to death, and to decay
verses.h2: their dwellings; their company is destined to break apart.

verses.h1: So be patient; if lamentation and sorrow can restore
verses.h2: to you what has passed, then give way to grief.

verses.h1: طال الثواء على رسم بتمثود
verses.h2: أودي، وكل جديد مرة مود

verses.h1: دار الفتاة التي كنا نقول لها
verses.h2: يا ظبية عطلا حسانة الجيد

verses.h1: Long have I lingered by the traces at Tamthūd;
verses.h2: they have perished—and all that is new must one day perish.

verses.h1: The abode of the girl to whom we used to say:
verses.h2: “O unadorned gazelle, so lovely of neck!”

notes.note: Tamthūd (تمثود) is an unidentified place; its vocalization is uncertain.
طال الثواء literally means “the stay has grown long,” without an explicit personal subject. It may describe the speaker’s lingering at the ruins, as translated, or the long passage of time over them.

verses.h1: ولقد نهيت الدمع يوم سويقة
verses.h2: فأبت غوالب عبرة ما تلب

verses.h1: عفت الرسوم، وما عفت أحشاؤه
verses.h2: من عهد شوق ما يزول فيذهب

verses.h1: ولو أنني أنصفت في حكم الهوى
verses.h2: ما شمت بارقة ورأسي أشيب

verses.h1: I bade my tears cease that day at Suwayqa,
verses.h2: but an overpowering flood of tears refused [text unclear].

verses.h1: The traces have faded, but his heart is not emptied
verses.h2: of an old longing that will not cease and pass away.

verses.h1: Had I judged fairly in matters of love,
verses.h2: I would not have watched for lightning with my head already gray.

notes.note: The closing words ما تلب are unclear and may be corrupted; they are not translated. Suwayqa is a place name, but its precise location here is uncertain.

أحشاؤه literally means ‘his inward parts,’ rendered here as ‘his heart.’ The third-person pronoun has no explicit antecedent in this excerpt and contrasts with the first person in the surrounding lines.

verses.h1: سل الأيام عن أمم تقضت
verses.h2: ستخبرك المعالم والرسوم

verses.h1: تنام ولم تنم عنك المنايا
verses.h2: تنبه للمنية يا نئوم

verses.h1: تروم الخلد في دار المنايا
verses.h2: وكم قد رام قبلك ما تروم

verses.h1: ألا يأيها الملك المرجى
verses.h2: عليك نواهض الدنيا تحوم

verses.h1: لأمر ما تصرفت الليالي
verses.h2: وأمر ما تقلبت النجوم

verses.h1: Ask the days about peoples who have passed away;
verses.h2: the landmarks and traces will tell you.

verses.h1: You sleep, but death does not sleep, unmindful of you;
verses.h2: awaken to death, you heavy sleeper.

verses.h1: You seek immortality in the abode of death;
verses.h2: how many before you have sought what you seek!

verses.h1: O king in whom hopes are placed,
verses.h2: the world’s winged perils hover over you.

verses.h1: For some purpose the nights have changed,
verses.h2: and for some purpose the stars have turned.

notes.note: نواهض الدنيا evokes birds rising into flight. I have rendered it as a metaphor for looming worldly perils, but the precise reference is uncertain.
The second hemistich begins وأمر ما, without the preposition ل found in لأمر ما in the first. The translation assumes parallel meanings; a ل may have been omitted in transmission.

poems.poet_from_text: مالك بن معاوية بن سلمة القشيري
poems.intro: قال مالك بن معاوية بن سلمة القشيري:

poet.from_text: مالك بن معاوية بن سلمة القشيري

verses.h1: تذكرت من سلمى وذو الشوق ذاكر
verses.h2: وحاجة من لم تقض داء مخامر

verses.h1: تذكر ذي شوق وهاج صبابة
verses.h2: خيال سليمى والرسوم الدوائر

verses.h1: بجو كأن لم تحتلله، ولم يكن
verses.h2: لأهلك مبدي حوله ومحاضر

verses.h1: I called Salmā to mind—for one who longs remembers—
verses.h2: and an unfulfilled desire is a sickness that takes hold.

verses.h1: I remembered as a yearning man remembers; and longing was stirred
verses.h2: by Sulaymā’s phantom and the fading traces

verses.h1: at Jaww, as though you had never dwelt there, nor had there been
verses.h2: desert camps and settlements by the water for your people around it.

notes.note: The construction وحاجة من لم تقض is grammatically unclear as printed. I have provisionally understood it as an unfulfilled desire; the wording may be incomplete or miscopied.
Jaww (جو) may be a place-name here, but the word can also mean a low-lying tract or broad valley.
I read مبدي as مبدى, a desert camping place, contrasted with محاضر, settlements at watering places.

prose_translation.intro: Mālik ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Salama al-Qushayrī said:

verses.h1: فقولا لباقي رسم ميلاء باللوى
verses.h2: لوى الهضب بين المغر والمتخرم

verses.h1: عليك سلام أيها الرسم باللوى
verses.h2: وحييت مسؤولا وإن لم تكلم

verses.h1: بما كنت إذ ميلاء ميلاء، والهوى
verses.h2: جميع، وشعب الدار لم يتقسم

verses.h1: كما يتمنى من تمنى، ولا أرى
verses.h2: دواما من الدنيا لحي بأنعم

verses.h1: فإن يخل من ميلاء ربع فما خلا
verses.h2: بنات الهوى من حبها المتقدم

verses.h1: صحا من تصابي من لداتي وحبها
verses.h2: شريك المنايا خيض في اللحم والدم

verses.h1: Say, you two, to the surviving trace of Maylāʾ’s dwelling at al-Liwā—
verses.h2: Liwā al-Haḍb, between al-Maghr and al-Mutakharram:

verses.h1: “Peace be upon you, trace of a dwelling at al-Liwā!
verses.h2: May you be greeted as we question you, though you do not speak—

verses.h1: For what you were when Maylāʾ was Maylāʾ, and love
verses.h2: was undivided, and the household’s company had not scattered,

verses.h1: Just as anyone who wishes would wish. Yet I see
verses.h2: no lasting worldly bliss for any living soul.

verses.h1: If a dwelling stands empty of Maylāʾ, there is no lack,
verses.h2: in the offspring of desire, of my long-standing love for her.

verses.h1: Those of my peers who dallied in youthful love have sobered; but love for her
verses.h2: is death’s companion, mingled with flesh and blood.

notes.note: The places are unidentified; the vocalizations al-Haḍb, al-Maghr, and al-Mutakharram are provisional.

بنات الهوى literally means “daughters of desire.” Its precise referent and the syntax of فما خلا بنات الهوى are uncertain; the translation takes it as feelings or thoughts born of love that still retain the speaker’s old attachment.

تصابي is read as تصابى, “acted youthfully” or “dallied in youthful love.” خيض is taken in the sense “mixed” or “mingled.” The precise force of شريك المنايا, literally “a partner of deaths,” is uncertain; it may suggest that this love will remain until death.

prose_translation.intro: And Kaʿb ibn Mashhūr al-Mukhabbalī said:

verses.h1: عجبا لهجرك قبل تشتيت النوى
verses.h2: منا، ووصلك في التنائي أعجب

verses.h1: أني اهتديت، وما اهتديت لمعمد
verses.h2: من ليل عانة والثريا تجنب

verses.h1: عفت الرسوم وما عفت أحشاؤه
verses.h2: من عهد شوق ما يحول فيذهب

verses.h1: How strange your estrangement before distance parted
verses.h2: us; and stranger still your closeness when far away!

verses.h1: How did you find your way, without guidance, to a man worn down by love,
verses.h2: through the night at ʿĀna, while the Pleiades veered south?

verses.h1: The traces are effaced, but his heart has not been cleared
verses.h2: of an old longing that will not change and pass away.

notes.note: The wording is uncertain. I take لمعمد to mean ‘to a man worn down,’ with love understood from context. وما اهتديت literally means ‘and you did not find your way’; ‘without guidance’ is a tentative contextual rendering. The text may be corrupt.

verses.h1: أمن رسم تعفى أو رماد
verses.h2: وسحم كالحمامات الفراد

verses.h1: أطاعتك الشؤون فظلت صبا
verses.h2: كأن وكيفها واهي المزاد

verses.h1: وهل يشتاق مثلك في ديار
verses.h2: عفتها الريح والديم الغوادي

verses.h1: ذكرت بها سعاد فعجب جهلا
verses.h2: على رسم تسائل عن سعاد

verses.h1: Was it for an effaced trace, or ashes,
verses.h2: and blackened hearthstones like solitary doves,

verses.h1: that your tear ducts obeyed you and kept pouring,
verses.h2: their streaming like a leaking waterskin?

verses.h1: Does one like you feel longing amid dwellings
verses.h2: erased by wind and steady morning rains?

verses.h1: You remembered Suʿād there and foolishly turned aside
verses.h2: to a trace, asking after Suʿād.

notes.note: The source reads فعجب, which is difficult to construe here. The translation provisionally reads فعجت, ‘you turned aside,’ a likely copying or OCR error.

verses.h1: أمن آل هند بالشريف رسوم
verses.h2: دوارس منها حادث وقديم

verses.h1: محتها رياح الصيف بعدك والبلى
verses.h2: وأسحم رجاف العشي سجوم

verses.h1: عهدت بها هندا، وهند غريرة
verses.h2: عن الفحش بلهاء العتي نئوم

verses.h1: فشطت نوى عنك الديار فأصبحت
verses.h2: مناصب رضوى دونها وتسوم

verses.h1: Are these traces of Hind’s people at al-Sharīf,
verses.h2: fading away, some recent and some old?

verses.h1: Summer winds and decay have erased them since you left,
verses.h2: and dark clouds, thundering at dusk, pouring down rain.

verses.h1: I knew Hind there, when Hind was innocent,
verses.h2: unversed in lewdness, simple-hearted, much given to evening sleep.

verses.h1: Then distance carried those dwellings far from you, and now
verses.h2: the heights of Raḍwā and Tasūm lie between you and them.

notes.note: العتي is unclear and may be an OCR error for العشي, ‘evening.’ The translation ‘evening sleep’ follows that conjecture; the wording and grammatical grouping remain uncertain.
مناصب is rendered tentatively as ‘heights’; its precise topographical sense here is uncertain. تسوم (Tasūm) appears to be a mountain name, but its identification is uncertain.

prose_translation.intro: And Rabīʿa ibn Maqrūm al-Ḍabbī said:

verses.h1: تغير الرسم من سلمى بأجفار
verses.h2: وأقفرت من سليمى دمنة الدار

verses.h1: وقد تكون بها سلمى تخدثني
verses.h2: تساقط الحلى حاجاتي وأوطاري

verses.h1: ثم استمر بسلمى نية قذف
verses.h2: وسير منقضب الأقران مغيار

verses.h1: كأن قلبي غداة البيت منقسم
verses.h2: طارت به عصب شتى لأمصار

verses.h1: ولو تلف النوى من قد تشوقه
verses.h2: إذن قضيت لباناتي وأسراري

verses.h1: The traces Salmā left at Ajfār have changed,
verses.h2: and the dwelling’s remains lie empty of Sulaymā.

verses.h1: Once Salmā would be there, telling me,
verses.h2: like falling jewels, all that I wished and longed to hear.

verses.h1: Then a far-off destination carried Salmā away,
verses.h2: and a swift journey that severed the bonds of companionship.

verses.h1: It was as though my heart, on the morning of parting, were divided,
verses.h2: and scattered bands bore it away to different towns.

verses.h1: If separation would reunite those it has filled with longing,
verses.h2: then I would fulfill my needs and secret desires.

notes.note: تخدثني appears to be a misprint for تحدثني, ‘speaking to me.’ The syntax of تساقط الحلى حاجاتي وأوطاري is uncertain; the translation tentatively takes her words as falling like jewels and expressing what he wishes to hear.
The phrase منقضب الأقران مغيار is difficult. I tentatively understand الأقران as bonds or ties and مغيار as describing swift travel.
البيت, ‘the house,’ appears to be a misprint for البين, ‘parting,’ which is adopted in the translation.

verses.h1: أرسما جديدا من سعاد تجنب
verses.h2: عفت روضة الأجداد منها فيثقب

verses.h1: عفا آيه ريح الجنوب مع الصبا
verses.h2: وأسحم دان مزنه متصوب

verses.h1: عهدت بها سعدى وفي العيش غرة
verses.h2: فأصبح باقي ودها يتقضب

verses.h1: وقد غنيت سعدى نثيب بودها
verses.h2: ليالي لا يسطاع منها التجنب

verses.h1: Do you shun a fresh trace of Suʿād’s dwelling?
verses.h2: Her dwelling at Rawḍat al-Ajdād has faded away, and at Yathqub too.

verses.h1: The south wind, together with the east wind, effaced its signs,
verses.h2: and a dark cloudbank, its clouds hanging low and pouring rain.

verses.h1: I knew Saʿdā there when life was carefree;
verses.h2: now what remains of her affection is breaking apart.

verses.h1: Saʿdā once dwelt there, requiting me with her love,
verses.h2: on nights when keeping away from her was impossible.

notes.note: I take تجنب as a second-person verb, ‘do you shun.’ Rawḍat al-Ajdād and Yathqub appear to be place names; their precise identification and vocalization are uncertain.
The printed نثيب (‘we reward’) is difficult in context. The translation assumes تثيب (‘she rewards’), a likely dotting or OCR error, and reads غنيت as feminine غَنِيَتْ, ‘she dwelt.’

verses.h1: ألا أيها الرسم المحيل ألم تكن
verses.h2: بك الأنس الراضون والخيل رودا

verses.h1: وبيض العذارى في جميع، كأنها
verses.h2: نعاج الملا يلبس ريطا ومجسدا

verses.h1: فإني وتهيامي بهن لكالذي
verses.h2: إذا نال من صداء شربا ترددا

verses.h1: فإن كنت ذا عقل فأقصر عن الصبي
verses.h2: ولا تتبعن عينيك شعبا تبددا

verses.h1: O timeworn trace of a dwelling, were there not once
verses.h2: contented folk within you, and horses roaming,

verses.h1: And fair maidens gathered together, as though they were
verses.h2: wild does of al-Malā, wearing fine wraps and saffron-dyed cloth?

verses.h1: For I, in my lovesick longing for them, am like one
verses.h2: who, once he drinks from Ṣadāʾ, returns again and again.

verses.h1: If you have sense, desist from youthful infatuation,
verses.h2: and do not let your eyes follow a people scattered apart.

notes.note: رودا is taken to describe horses roaming or grazing; its precise vocalization and grammatical connection are uncertain.
الملا is taken as the place-name al-Malā, though it can also denote an open plain. مجسدا is understood as saffron-dyed cloth; a differently vocalized form can mean a garment worn next to the skin.
يلبس appears grammatically irregular here; the sense suggests يلبسن or تلبس, ‘wear,’ referring to the maidens or their comparison to wild does.
الصبي is read as الصبا, ‘youthful infatuation’ or ‘youthful folly,’ rather than الصبي, ‘the boy’; the spelling may be a transcription error.

verses.h1: أهاجك أم لا بالتناصف مربع
verses.h2: ورسم بأجراع الغديرين بلقع

verses.h1: ديار لليلى إذ نحل بها معا
verses.h2: وإذ نحن منها في المودة نطمع

verses.h1: فإن تك قد شطت نواها، وأن نأت
verses.h2: فإن النوى مما تشت وتجمع

verses.h1: Has a spring campsite at al-Tanāṣuf stirred your longing, or not,
verses.h2: and a desolate trace on the sandy flats of al-Ghadīrayn?

verses.h1: Dwellings of Laylā, where we once lodged together,
verses.h2: when we hoped for affection from her.

verses.h1: If her destination lies far away, and if she is distant,
verses.h2: separation can both part and reunite.

notes.note: Al-Tanāṣuf and al-Ghadīrayn are treated as place names; their precise locations are uncertain.
The source’s وأن نأت is read as وإن نأت (‘and if she is distant’), a likely spelling or transcription error.

verses.h1: لعزة من أيام ذي الغصن هاجني
verses.h2: بضاحي قرار الروضتين رسوم

verses.h1: هي الدار وحشا غير أن قد يحلها
verses.h2: ويغني بها شخص علي كريم

verses.h1: سألت حكيما: أين شطت بها النوى؟
verses.h2: فخبرني ما لا أحب حكيم

verses.h1: تمر السنون الماضيات ولا أرى
verses.h2: بصحن الشبا أطلالهن تريم

verses.h1: From ʿAzza’s days at Dhū al-Ghuṣn, I was stirred
verses.h2: by traces in the open hollow of al-Rawḍatayn.

verses.h1: That is the dwelling, desolate, though once there lodged
verses.h2: and lived someone dear to me.

verses.h1: I asked Ḥakīm: “Where has separation carried her so far away?”
verses.h2: And Ḥakīm told me what I did not wish to hear.

verses.h1: The years pass by, yet I do not see
verses.h2: their ruins disappear from the open ground of al-Shaba.

notes.note: Dhū al-Ghuṣn and al-Rawḍatayn are treated as place names; their precise locations are uncertain. قرار may mean a hollow or low-lying, level ground.
I read يغني as يغنى, ‘dwells,’ rather than ‘sings.’ The temporal force of قد يحلها is uncertain: the translation takes it as recalling a former inhabitant, but it could mean ‘may lodge there.’

The antecedent of ‘their’ in أطلالهن is unclear in this quotation. Al-Shaba is treated as a place name, but its precise identification and vocalization are uncertain. تريم literally means ‘move away’ or ‘depart,’ rendered here as ‘disappear.’

verses.h1: أحادرة دموعك دار مي
verses.h2: وهائجة صبابتك الرسوم

verses.h1: عفت وعهودها متقادمات
verses.h2: وقد يبقى لك العهد القديم

verses.h1: وقد يمسي الجميع أولو المحاوي
verses.h2: بها المتجاور الحلل المقيم

verses.h1: Does Mayy’s dwelling draw down your tears,
verses.h2: and do its traces stir your longing?

verses.h1: They have faded, and the days spent there are long past,
verses.h2: yet an old memory may still remain with you.

verses.h1: Once the whole tribe, the people of the tent-circles, would pass the evening
verses.h2: there, settled in neighboring camps.

verses.h1: لم يبق بعدكم رسم ولا طلل
verses.h2: إلا وللبين في تغييره عمل

verses.h1: غبتم فأوحشتم الدنيا لغيبتكم
verses.h2: فاليوم لا عوض منكم ولا بدل

verses.h1: حملتموني على ضعفي بفرقتكم
verses.h2: ما ليس يحمله سهل ولا جبل

verses.h1: إذا شممت نسيما من دياركم
verses.h2: عدمت عقلي، كأني شارب ثمل

verses.h1: Since you left, no trace or ruin remains
verses.h2: that separation has not worked to alter.

verses.h1: You went away, and your absence made the world desolate;
verses.h2: now nothing can replace you or make up for your loss.

verses.h1: By leaving, you burdened me, despite my weakness,
verses.h2: with what neither plain nor mountain can bear.

verses.h1: Whenever I breathe a breeze from your dwellings,
verses.h2: I lose my reason, like a man drunk on wine.

verses.h1: أصبا الأصائل إن برقة ثهمد
verses.h2: تشكوا اختلافك بالهبوب السرمد

verses.h1: لا تبغني عرصاتها إن الهوى
verses.h2: ملقى على تلك الرسوم الهمد

verses.h1: دمن مواثل كالنجوم، فإن عفت
verses.h2: فبأي نجم في الصبابة نهتدي؟

verses.h1: O east wind of late afternoon, Burqat Thahmad
verses.h2: complains of your ceaseless visits, blowing upon it.

verses.h1: Do no violence in its courts, for love
verses.h2: lies cast upon those lifeless traces.

verses.h1: Remnants standing clear as stars; if they are effaced,
verses.h2: by what star shall we find our way in longing?

notes.note: The wording لا تبغني عرصاتها is unclear and may be corrupted. The translation provisionally reads لا تبغ في عرصاتها, ‘do no violence in its courts,’ continuing the address to the wind.

verses.h1: ولقد وقفت على الرسوم فلم أجد
verses.h2: عتبا على سكب الدموع الذرف

verses.h1: وسألتها حين انجذبت فلم تصخ
verses.h2: فيه لدعوة عاشق مستوقف

verses.h1: دمن جنيت بها الهوى من غصنه
verses.h2: وسحبت فيها اللهو سحب المطرف

verses.h1: فلأجرين الدمع إن لم تجره
verses.h2: ولأعرفن الوجد إن لم تعرف

verses.h1: I stood at the traces and found
verses.h2: no cause for reproach in shedding streaming tears.

verses.h1: I questioned them when I was drawn to them, but they would not listen
verses.h2: then to the call of a lover asking for a halt.

verses.h1: Ruins where I plucked love from its branch
verses.h2: and trailed pleasure like a bordered cloak.

verses.h1: I shall surely make tears flow if they shed none,
verses.h2: and surely know longing if they do not.

notes.note: حين انجذبت is unclear in context: literally, ‘when I was drawn’ (or ‘when she/it was drawn’). ‘To them’ is supplied tentatively. The reference of فيه, rendered ‘then,’ is also uncertain; the wording may be corrupt.
The unvocalized مستوقف is taken as active, ‘asking for a halt’; it could instead be passive, describing a lover who has been stopped or detained.
تجره and تعرف can refer to the ruins or address someone as ‘you.’ The translation takes the ruins as their subject.

verses.h1: ألا حي بالزرق الرسوم الخواليا
verses.h2: وإن لم تكن إلا رميما بواليا

verses.h1: عفت برهة أطلال مي وأدرجت
verses.h2: بها الريح تحت الغيم قطرا وسافيا

verses.h1: تحمل منها أهل مي فودعوا
verses.h2: بها أهلها لا ينظرون التواليا

verses.h1: وقد كنت من مي إذ الحي جيرة
verses.h2: على البخل منها ميت القلب ساهيا

verses.h1: Come, greet the deserted traces at al-Zurq,
verses.h2: though they are nothing but crumbling, weathered remains.

verses.h1: Over time, Mayy’s ruined campsite faded; the wind swept
verses.h2: rain and drifting dust across it beneath the clouds.

verses.h1: Mayy’s people departed from there, bidding farewell
verses.h2: there to its inhabitants, not waiting for those who trailed behind.

verses.h1: In those days with Mayy, when the tribe lived as neighbors,
verses.h2: despite her withholding, I was dead at heart and heedless.

notes.note: Al-Zurq appears to be a place-name; its precise identification is uncertain.

The referent of أهلها (‘its inhabitants’) is unclear after the mention of Mayy’s departing people. لا ينظرون التواليا may mean ‘not looking toward those behind’ rather than ‘not waiting for those who trailed behind.’

The emotional force of ميت القلب ساهيا (literally, ‘dead-hearted, heedless’) in describing his relationship with Mayy is uncertain. Her ‘withholding’ presumably concerns affection or favor, though this is not explicit.

verses.h1: بكيت وما أبكاني الرسم إذ عفا
verses.h2: ولا الربع أضحى نويه وهو دائر

verses.h1: ولكنني لا أستفيق تذكرا
verses.h2: وليس بمنفك من الدمع ذاكر

verses.h1: I wept, but it was not the faded traces that made me weep,
verses.h2: nor the campsite, its enclosing trench now effaced.

verses.h1: Rather, remembering, I cannot regain my senses;
verses.h2: and one who remembers is never free of tears.

notes.note: نويه probably represents نؤيه, ‘its trench’ (dug around a campsite to divert rainwater). The construction أضحى نويه وهو دائر is awkward and possibly corrupt; the translation takes دائر in the sense ‘effaced’ rather than ‘circular.’

poems.intro: قال تبارك وتعالى: (إنا نحن نحيي الموتى، ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم) . قيل: نحييهم بالإيمان بعد الكفر، وقيل: بالبعث، "ونكتب ما قدموا": ما عملوا من خير أو شر. "وآثارهم" ما أثروا من سنة حسنة، وسيرة يعمل بها بعدهم، وقيل: "آثارهم": خطاهم إلى المساجد. وروى سفيان، عن أبي نضرة، عن أبي سعيد الخدري - رحمهم الله - قال: "كانت بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة، فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قريب من المسجد فنزلت: (إنا نحن نحيي الموتى، ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم) فقال لهم النبي: "إن آثاركم تكتب" فلم ينتقلوا. وقد روى عن أبي سعيد الخدري - رحمه الله - أن بني سلمة شكوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد منازلهم من المسجد، فأنزل الله سبحانه: (إنا نحن نحيي الموتى، ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم) فقالوا: عليكم منازلكم، فإنما تكتب آثاركم. وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز - رضوان الله عليه -: لو كان الله تعالى مغفلا شيئا لأغفل هذه الآثار التي تعفوها الرياح. يعني قوله عز وجل: (إنا نحن نحيي الموتى، ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم) . قال الأحوص:

verses.h1: ضوء نار بدا لعينيك أم شب
verses.h2: بت بذي الأثل من سلامة نار

verses.h1: تلك بين الرياض والأثل والبا
verses.h2: نات منا ومن سلامة دار

verses.h1: وكذاك الزمان يذهب بالنا
verses.h2: س، وتبقى الرسوم والآثار

verses.h1: Was it firelight that appeared to your eyes, or was there kindled
verses.h2: at Dhū al-Athl a fire of Salāma’s?

verses.h1: There, among the meadows, tamarisks, and bān trees,
verses.h2: is a dwelling once ours and Salāma’s.

verses.h1: So does time carry people away,
verses.h2: while the outlines and traces remain.

notes.note: I read شب / بت, split across the hemistichs, as شُبِّبَت, ‘was kindled.’ The contrast between the opening firelight and Salāma’s fire is unclear.
Dhū al-Athl is an unidentified place.
الرياض والأثل والبانات are translated as landscape terms (‘meadows, tamarisks, and bān trees’); some or all may instead be place-names: Al-Riyāḍ, al-Athl, and al-Bānāt.

prose_translation.intro:
He—blessed and exalted—said: “Indeed, We give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and the traces they leave behind.” It has been said: We give them life through faith after unbelief; and it has been said: through resurrection. “And We record what they have sent ahead”: whatever good or evil they have done. “And the traces they leave behind”: whatever good practice they have established, and a way of conduct that is followed after them. It has also been said that “the traces they leave behind” means their footsteps to the mosques.

Sufyān related, from Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī—may God have mercy on them—who said: “Banū Salima lived in an outlying part of al-Madina and wished to move nearer the mosque. Then the verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, We give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and the traces they leave behind.’ The Prophet said to them, ‘Your footsteps are indeed recorded,’ so they did not move.”
